conviction_note: No option anchor, so abs_move_pct is the name's own median reaction (11.57%) nudged to 12 for a going-concern balance sheet, a ~20%-of-shares short and a back-loaded guide; p_up 46 is a faint down lean from a 6-of-7 down reaction history and the funding gap, pulled toward 50 by the crowded short, a 69% drawdown since August and a guide the company reaffirmed after Q3 closed. The findings sum to +0.25 and the scaled number to -0.96. They differ in sign because the per-finding sizes net a confirmed guide hold and possible balance-sheet actions against the cash gap, while p_up also carries this stock's habit of selling prints, which no single finding holds.
bar: No sourced Q3 2026 consensus. Yahoo shows no estimates (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MVIS/analysis), and the Q2 estimate itself was disputed: $3.38m per Benzinga against $1.0m per a MarketBeat preview (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/microvision-mvis-expected-to-announce-quarterly-earnings-on-thursday-2026-07-30/). The only sourced bar is the company's FY2026 revenue guide of $10-15m, reaffirmed 2026-10-07 after Q3 had closed (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm). The Q2 call's prepared remarks said $10-16m, read back in Q&A as $10-15m (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/668269-q2-2026/). H1 revenue was $2.4m (Q1 $0.9m, Q2 $1.5m), so the guide implies $7.6-12.6m in H2. print_vs_bar_pct is my Q3 revenue estimate (~$2.7m) against a pro-rata Q3 share (~$3.0m) of the low end of that implied H2. Because the bar is unsourced, every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest about 6.2m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 4.3 days to cover (5.7m and 4.9 days on 09-15), per Curved Trading citing FINRA (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mvis/short-interest/, seen via search snippet; the page returned 403 to fetch). That is about 20.5% of the 30.15m shares outstanding at 2026-08-14 (per the 13G at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000205845126000002/primary_doc.xml), so the short is crowded, though part of it is likely a hedge by the convertible-note holder and the warrant holders. No usable option chain, so there is no 25d skew. Put/call OI is 0.77 on 607 contracts total, which is negligible. Tape: spot $1.23, -18% over 20 days, 8.9% above the 52-week low, -93% from the 52-week high. A third-party price table puts the low at $1.08 on 2026-10-19 (https://www.macroaxis.com/microvision-stock-price).

findings.finding: The company reaffirmed FY2026 revenue of $10-15m and guided 2027 revenue to double on 2026-10-07, after Q3 had closed: the CFO said 'we are confident in our ability to meet the full year guidance in the range of $10 million-$15 million', and management said it was 'shipping sensors until the last day of the quarter to maximize revenue'. A guide cut at this print is therefore less likely than the name's history of missed street numbers implies (Q2 revenue $1.47m against a $3.38m estimate).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reaffirmation itself was sold: a third-party price table shows the stock -13.8% on 4.6m shares on 2026-10-08, the session after the 16:05 ET 8-K. In the baseline, prints that carried guidance (03-04 -29.5%, 05-13 -21.1%) were sold hard; the 08-06 print that reiterated the guide and raised gross margin rose 4.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and the stock fell on it, so the statement itself is priced. What may not be priced is that it was made with Q3 already known. If the market believed a hold at the print, the stock would not sit 8.9% off its 52-week low at about $37m market cap against a guide that implies H2 revenue 3-5x H1. The guide sits inside what the company already told the market, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript, prepared remarks: 'more revenue coming Q3' from the MicroVision Semiconductor project, and Lake Fusion 'unit sales that are occurring here in Q3' (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/668269-q2-2026/). The investor-update transcript (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/761601-investor-update/) is the same event as the 8-K exhibit and counts once.

findings.finding: The cash runway does not reach year-end without more equity. Cash was $27.2m on 2026-06-30. The $17.0m gross unit offering of 6.8m shares plus 6.8m warrants at $2.50 netted $15.6m on 2026-08-17. Against that sit about $60m of FY2026 burn guidance, of which $35.6m of operating cash was used in H1, and convertible-note redemptions scheduled at $19.8m for the rest of 2026 ($3.0m a month plus a 10% premium). The 10-Q carries going-concern language and a minimum-cash covenant of the lesser of $17.5m or 110% of the note balance. The offering's 45-day lock-up on new issuance and note repayments ended about 2026-10-01, leaving $41.2m of ATM availability. On my walk, Q3-end cash is roughly $25-30m and Q4 needs ATM sales or note conversions into stock, which the Q3 10-Q cover share count will show.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-14/17 offering at $2.50 coincided with a reported -40.7% session (search snippet); the stock is now $1.23, below the $2.50 offer and warrant strike. Every print in the baseline after a dilution-heavy quarter was down (03-04 -29.5%, 05-13 -21.1%).
findings.why_not_priced: The going-concern flag and the August raise are public, and the 69% drawdown since August shows much of this is in the price. What the market cannot yet see is the size of post-lock-up ATM and conversion issuance in October and the Q3-end cash figure against the $17.5m covenant. If that were priced, the stock would trade near the cash-adjusted value with no further drift, rather than having set a new low ($1.08 on 10-19) after the lock-up ended. Rule 4 answer: the money funds operating losses and note redemptions, not a corroborated ramp (H1 revenue $2.4m against $60m of burn), so the sign is negative. It is shrunk for the roughly 20% short interest.
findings.independence: The offering terms are a separate primary document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226038743/form8-k.htm. The Q2 call confirms $41.2m of ATM capacity and the covenant (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mvis/transcripts/668269-q2-2026/).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is at risk of landing below whatever street number exists, because the company's own guide is back-loaded. H1 revenue was $2.4m, and the guide needs $7.6-12.6m in H2. On the Q2 call the CEO said MOVIA S has 'not a large revenue portion for 2026' (launched in late October, after Q3) and that IRIS supply was 'more of a timing issue... Q3 or Q4 of this year or Q1 or Q2 of next year'. Q2 revenue missed the $3.38m estimate by 56%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed by 56% and the stock rose 4.0% over the print window (08-06), because the guide and the gross-margin raise carried it. Earlier revenue disappointments (03-04, 05-13) were sold 21-30%.
findings.why_not_priced: No published Q3 consensus exists, so the market has no stated number to be wrong against, and that is why this is capped small. If the back-loading were fully priced, the 10-07 'confident in guidance' statement would not have needed to be made. It is an inference from the company's own phasing comments, not a counted number.
findings.independence: Benzinga Q2 actual against estimate ($1.47m against $3.38m), via search snippet: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MVIS/earnings. It partly pulls against finding 1: both rest on the same guide but land on different lines (Q3 actual against FY guide hold).

findings.finding: Management pre-announced balance-sheet actions to be detailed 'in the next few weeks as we come up to our Q3 earnings call': a second phase of operating-expense cuts, a review of 'our debt structure and lease obligations', and 'non-core assets... that we could monetize'. A concrete asset sale, note restructuring or opex number at the print would be the first non-dilutive liquidity source on a going-concern name.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print announced an asset sale or debt restructuring. The 05-13 print, which announced a 15% workforce cut and a burn reduction from $65-70m to $60m, still fell 21.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The intention is public. The content (a dollar figure for a monetization or debt amendment) is not, and the stock fell to new lows after the update, so the market has given the intention no credit. If it had, the stock would not have set a new low on 10-19. Sized small because the history shows cost-cut news on this name has not been bought.
findings.independence: Same event as the 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm), which also mentions evaluating debt structure, leases and non-core asset sales; one source, counted once.

findings.finding: The short is crowded into the print at about 6.2m shares short (2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 4.3 days to cover), roughly 20% of the 30.15m shares outstanding, while a single individual (Johannes Gnauck / JG Global LLC) disclosed a 7.9% long stake (2.38m shares) on a 13G with event date 2026-09-16. That is a squeeze mechanism on any non-negative surprise in a $37m stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows only one up print in seven (+4.0% on 08-06); no squeeze on a print is visible in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: The short is part of the price, but its asymmetry is not: with 4.3 days to cover and borrowable supply competing with ATM issuance, a good-news print would require covering into thin float. Part of the short is likely a hedge by the note and warrant holders and will not cover, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: The short interest figure comes via search snippet (Curved Trading citing FINRA): https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mvis/short-interest/

outside_window.finding: Listing risk returns. Spot is $1.23, 23% above the $1 Nasdaq bid floor that MVIS regained compliance with on 2026-08-26, after a 1-for-15 reverse split effective 2026-08-01. Another deficiency needs 30 consecutive sessions below $1, which cannot occur inside this window.

Monthly convertible-note partial redemptions ($3.0m plus a 10% premium, about $19.8m scheduled for the rest of 2026, maturity March 2028) keep producing conversion share supply or cash drain into Q4 and beyond.

lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced: no Q3 consensus, and the Q2 estimates disagreed): capped every finding small; the guidance finding sits inside what the company already guided, so it went from +1.0 to +0.5.
Rule 7 (crowded short at about 20% of shares, 4.3 days to cover): the financing negative shrank from -1.5 to -1.0.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): answered. The money funds losses and note redemptions with a going-concern flag and no corroborated ramp, so the sign stays negative.
Rule 5 (inference from phasing comments rather than a counted number): Q3 revenue risk went from -1.0 to -0.75.
Rule 1 (this name sells its prints, 6 of 7 down): the balance-sheet-action and positioning positives each went from +1.0 to +0.75; p_up moved from 45 to 46 net of the squeeze argument.
Rule 6 window: the listing-risk and note-redemption items stayed in outside_window.
